subject: Rolling roster update: edge-agent processor consolidation & evidence request
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, EdgeAgent Ops <ops@edgeagent.ai>, RegulaSec Compliance <compliance@regulasec.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Jun 2029 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Rolling roster update: edge-agent processor consolidation & evidence request

Hi all,

Quick heads-up: EdgeAgent is planning a rolling consolidation of several telemetry/processing partners into their new "edge-agent" processor (target cutover window: 2029-07-15 to 2029-07-22). Per our DPA obligations with customers in the EU and APAC, we need
- a short inventory of processing locations
- clear documentation of what data types the processor sees (logs, telemetry, PII-derived IDs)
- encryption/key custody information and egress routes

I've attached a short consolidation_summary.pdf and an export of the current roster (roster_export_20290611.csv) they shared. Can EdgeAgent confirm the following by EOD Tue 2029-06-18?
1) Primary processing regions for the consolidated processor.
2) Whether any logs or trace identifiers will transit outside of the listed regions (explicit country list).
3) KMS/HSM provider and whether keys are customer-isolated or shared.
4) Any subcontractors (names + country) that will have access to raw telemetry.

Kimberly / Soojin — please flag any customers you expect to be impacted by this change (especially EU-resident customers) and whether we should request a temporary mitigation (routing to legacy processor).

Markus — legal has asked for a brief amendment if any new subprocessors are introduced; I will prepare the draft once we get the processor roster and residency answers.

Thanks — Mina

-- 
Mina Haddad
Director, Product Security
Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.ai
(Attachment: consolidation_summary.pdf, roster_export_20290611.csv)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, EdgeAgent Ops <ops@edgeagent.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 Jun 2029 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Rolling roster update: edge-agent processor consolidation & evidence request

Thanks Mina — quick clarifying Qs:
- Are we expecting any EU customers to move from onshore to offshore processing as part of this consolidation? If so, can we get a per-customer mapping (even a short list)?
- For the short term, would EdgeAgent accept a canary/route pin for identified customers to keep them on the legacy processor?

Operational asks from our side:
- If they will touch logs with user identifiers, we should get a log retention window and delete policy.
- If any subcontractor is outside the EU, we need explicit export/safeguard descriptions (SCCs, encryption-in-transit guarantees).

EdgeAgent team — can you confirm whether the new processor will inherit the existing contract terms and SOC/Security attestations from the previous provider, or will this be a new attestation cohort? We need that to decide whether an amendment is required vs. a notification.

Kimberly

--
Kimberly Park
Senior Manager, Security & Privacy
Redwood Inference

From: RegulaSec Compliance <compliance@regulasec.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, EdgeAgent Ops <ops@edgeagent.ai>
Date: Thu, 13 Jun 2029 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Rolling roster update: edge-agent processor consolidation & evidence request

Hi Mina / EdgeAgent —

Thanks for the notice. Quick answers inline and attachments included: regulasec_attestation_summary.pdf, s3-egress-map.png.

1) Processing regions: primary processing occurs in us-west-2 and eu-central-1.
2) Transit: short-lived shards for cache invalidation are routed through sgp1 (Singapore) for edge performance; those shards contain only hashed IDs and time-series metrics, not raw PII. We have provided the s3-egress-map.png to show data flows.
3) Keys: We use Vault + customer-scoped KMS keys; production keys are in AWS KMS (customer-specific master keys are supported but require additional onboarding).
4) Subprocessors: currently, the consolidated processor will engage two additional partners for CDN/edge caching (CacheVista Ltd. — Singapore, and FastMirror GmbH — DE). Both are covered under our master subprocessors list — attestation included.

Note: we can provide a short scoped SOC2-plus report for the edge-agent processor within 10 business days if Redwood requires a fresh attestation. Otherwise, the existing attestation (attached) covers the controls in scope.

If you need explicit contract language for an amendment, we can provide suggested wording for a one-paragraph amendment referencing the subprocessors and residency guarantees.

Best,
Liam O'Connor
Head of Compliance
RegulaSec
(compliance@regulasec.com)

Appreciate the quick turnaround, Liam — this helps a lot. Next steps from Redwood:

- Markus will draft a one-paragraph amendment referencing CacheVista Ltd. and FastMirror GmbH and the residency commitments; sending the draft to EdgeAgent legal today. (Attachment: amendment_draft.docx)
- RegulaSec — we'd like the scoped SOC2-plus in written form if you can get it in 10 business days; otherwise please confirm the specific control gaps (if any) that would impact GDPR residency/processor obligations.

I've opened a short shared folder with the diagram and supporting files: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cEdgeRosterDiagram

Mina
